title: Transistor Ideal-Degree Lower-Bound Conjecture
summary: The Transistor analysis conjectures a lower bound on the ideal degree of its Gröbner-basis polynomial system; proving or refuting that bound remains open.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of Transistor through a Gröbner-basis attack on a zero-dimensional polynomial ideal.
parameters: I: the zero-dimensional ideal of the polynomial system modeling Transistor's first clocks
15: degree of each independent equation and base of the conjectured lower bound
16: number of independent degree-15 equations and exponent of the conjectured lower bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that the ideal degree is at least 15^16, approximately 2^62.5.

progress.summary: The paper presents the ideal-degree lower bound as a conjecture attributed to [69]. It treats the bound as underlying the asserted cost of change-of-order algorithms.
citation_labels: Jules Baudrin et al., Transistor: a TFHE-friendly Stream Cipher
